rounds.proof_sketch: For input [128, 4000] with dim=1: inner_size = 1 → grid_x = ceil(1/256) = 1 → blockIdx.x ∈ {0}. With blockIdx.x = 0: original = 0 * 256 + threadIdx.x = threadIdx.x; mutated = 0 * 1 + threadIdx.x = threadIdx.x. Both identical.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation replaces blockDim.x (256) with blockDim.z (1) in the inner_idx calculation. However, since inner_size = 1 for the fixed input shape [128, 4000] with dim=1, the grid only has one block in the x-dimension (grid_x = 1). This means blockIdx.x is always 0 for all threads. When multiplied by 0, both 256 and 1 produce 0, making the expressions semantically equivalent. The difference would only manifest if inner_size > 256, requiring blockIdx.x > 0, but this requires changing either the tensor shape or the dim parameter.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. Would require changing to dim=0 (making inner_size=4000, grid_x=16) or changing the shape to have dimensions after the cumsum axis summing to >256.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for GPU kernels should consider kernel launch parameters as part of the configuration space. When index calculations involve products like `blockIdx.x * blockDim.x`, mutations to either factor may be masked when the other factor is 0. Testing should include shape configurations that exercise all grid dimensions > 1.
